# Gilbert Blythe

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-two  <sub>[v1 c1 P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023), [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c40 P22](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0022), [v3 c41 P0](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v3 c1 P0](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Medical Student / Formerly Teacher  <sub>[v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v3 c7 P13](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0013), [v3 c41 P36](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0036)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Gil  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Gilbert is a tall, handsome young man with hazel eyes, curly brown hair, a strong chin, and a teasing, roguish smile. In his early teens he possessed an athletic, well-built frame, though later in his college years he appeared taller, more manly, and occasionally pale or thin due to overwork and illness. During a college initiation, he famously paraded in a calico kitchen apron and sunbonnet while retaining his courtly posture.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v3 c5 P1](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0001), [v3 c34 P11](../source/v03-c34.md#nw-v03-c34-p0011), [v3 c36 P22](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0022), [v3 c37 P28](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0028)_

## Personality

Gilbert is intelligent, ambitious, and hardworking, holding high ideals about his duty to society and his future profession. He possesses a quick wit, a teasing sense of humor, and a cheerful, friendly disposition, making him popular among his peers. Though competitive and determined to excel academically, he is inherently generous, fair-minded, and self-sacrificing. His deep capacity for devotion is shown by his steadfast loyalty to Anne Shirley through years of misunderstanding and unspoken love.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c7 P13](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0013), [v2 c7 P14](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0014), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v2 c19 P52](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0052)_

## History

Gilbert grew up in Avonlea but spent three years in Alberta with his father before returning to Avonlea School at age fourteen. On his first afternoon back, he jokingly pulled Anne Shirley's red braid and called her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Though he immediately apologized, Anne nursed a grudge for years, ignoring his repeated attempts at reconciliation, including rescuing her when her dory sank during a play of 'Elaine.' Gilbert competed fiercely with Anne for top honors at school and Queen's Academy, where both graduated into the fifth class and eventually tied for first place on the Entrance Examinations. Upon graduating from Queen's, Gilbert voluntarily gave up his appointment as teacher of the Avonlea school so that Anne could remain at Green Gables with Marilla after Matthew's death, accepting the White Sands school instead. He later attended Redmond College, becoming Freshman Class President, captain of the football team, and winner of the prestigious Cooper Prize in Classics. During his Junior year, he proposed to Anne at Patty's Place but was refused, leading to a period of distant friendship. Following graduation, Gilbert fell dangerously ill with typhoid fever in Avonlea, but recovered, after which he reconciled with Anne during a walk to Hester Gray's garden, where she accepted his proposal of marriage.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c15 P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 c15 P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c28 P23](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0023), [v1 c28 P31](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0031), [v1 c32 P40](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0040), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031), [v3 c39 P23](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0023), [v3 c40 P6](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0006), [v3 c40 P25](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0025), [v3 c41 P24](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0024), [v3 c41 P38](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0038)_

## Background by volume

- Son of John Blythe and Mrs. Blythe of Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037), [v3 c23 P0](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0000)</sub>
- Lived in Alberta for three years during his youth due to his father's health  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- Attended Avonlea School and Queen's Academy before going to Redmond College  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c17 P37](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0037), [v3 c3 P11](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0011)</sub>
- Taught school at White Sands for a year to earn money for college  <sub>[v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>

## Quotes

> I'm awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne. Honest I am. Don't be mad for keeps, now.  <sub>[v1 c15 P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)</sub>

> It's a splendid profession. A fellow has to fight something all through life . . . didn't somebody once define man as a fighting animal? . . . and I want to fight disease and pain and ignorance . . .  <sub>[v2 c7 P13](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0013)</sub>

> Friends! Your friendship can't satisfy me, Anne. I want your love—and you tell me I can never have that.  <sub>[v3 c20 P41](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0041)</sub>

> I asked you a question over two years ago, Anne. If I ask it again today will you give me a different answer?  <sub>[v3 c41 P24](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0024)</sub>

> There was nobody else—there never could be anybody else for me but you. I've loved you ever since that day you broke your slate over my head in school.  <sub>[v3 c41 P29](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0029)</sub>
